title: Macron says CIA did not warn French intelligence of possible Russian drone attacks
detail: French President Emmanuel Macron stated that the CIA did not inform French intelligence services about possible Russian drone attacks, raising concerns about intelligence-sharing gaps within NATO. The disclosure highlights friction in transatlantic information-sharing arrangements and comes amid heightened alertness over Russian hybrid operations targeting European infrastructure.

title: Danish intelligence warns of rising risk of limited Russian attack on a NATO state as Rutte urges calm
detail: The Danish Defence Intelligence Service (DDIS) warned that Russia has become more willing to take risks and assessed a low but growing risk of a limited military attack against a NATO member bordering Russia within the coming months, potentially disguised as an accidental weapons deviation blamed on jamming. DDIS separately warned that Russian hybrid-war activity — sabotage, destructive cyberattacks and drone incursions — is likely to escalate against European and NATO targets, while finding no evidence the Kremlin is preparing an outright invasion, which it said would require at least six months' visible preparation. Speaking hours later in New York, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance has "all these response options in place" and that citizens of the 32 member states "can remain calm," arguing the rise in hybrid incidents shows Vladimir Putin is "in a bad place" in Ukraine and that the best response is more weapons for Ukrainian forces.

media.caption: European security officials assess Russian sabotage surge poses no imminent NATO military threat
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte says the alliance can remain calm and has response options in place
